correctness.rationale: The language permits integer linear comparisons and negation. For each n≥1 one depth-one child has X~Bin(n,1/2), and B is 2X=n or 2X=n+1; exactly one equality is feasible for any parity, giving q_n=2^(−n)binom(n,ceil(n/2)). The n child leaf blocks are independent, so root Ψ=(#B=0) has exact probability (1−q_n)^n. Stirling gives q_n=sqrt(2/(πn))(1+O(1/n)); nq_n→∞, proving μ_n→0, and n log(1−q_n)=−sqrt(2n/π)−1/π+O(n^(−1/2)) via n q_n^2/2→1/π and n q_n^3=O(n^(−1/2)). Under the original paper’s recursive Definition 6.3, the depth-one B limit is 0, so #B=0 has substituted probability 1 for every outer n and μ′_∞=1. Depth-one probabilities coincide by original definition, and without propositional letters fixed-depth comparisons of eventually 0/n successor counts stabilize as the sign of integer affine expressions, proving zero-letter impossibility. The maximal gap is bounded by probabilities in [0,1]. Independently enumerated all 2^(n²) leaf valuations for n=1,2,3,4, obtaining 1/2,1/4,125/512,625/4096 exactly. Numeric residuals log μ_n + sqrt(2n/π) at n=100,1000,10000 were −0.314677,−0.317297,−0.318003, tending toward −1/π≈−0.318310. Enumeration and numerics are corroboration only, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The advertised refutation of Ghosh–Schwarzentruber’s adherence conjecture with maximal unit discrepancy is already established by the published 2026-11-02 Poisson-amplification theorem: its (k,t)=(1,1) depth-two formula has ordinary probability tending to one and recursive-limit probability zero, and its negation reverses those endpoints. The published 2026-11-08 one-letter parity-spectrum theorem is stronger at the crucial alphabet restriction: writing θ_0=(#p-#¬p=0), θ_1=(#p-#¬p=1), C_a=#θ_a, the assigned B is θ_0∨θ_1 and Ψ is ¬[(C_0≥1)∨(C_1≥1)]. That Boolean formula belongs to the prior one-letter fragment. The earlier paper’s exact π_{n,a} law and nπ_{n,a}~sqrt(2n/π) show the ordinary limit is zero on BOTH parities; the original arXiv Definition 6.3 supplies surrogate one. Its exact finite expression is immediate from those same per-category probabilities. The remaining -1/π logarithmic term is routine Stirling-plus-log expansion, while the zero-letter and depth-one lower bounds follow directly from the semantics. The exact expression may not appear verbatim in either older RESULT, but novelty is assessed by mathematical implication; no independently substantive claim survives.
residual_risks: The two 2026-11-08 findings share a calendar date, so exact within-day ordering is not established; the 2026-11-02 counterexample plainly predates the assigned record, and current mathematical coverage remains decisive.

The published one-variable spectrum theorem does not spell out this exact Ψ or its −1/π second term verbatim; its exact category formulas and uniform limiting assertions imply them as elementary specializations.

The original paper elsewhere mentions bounded rather than full branching; all checked counterexamples, including the submitted formula and prior Results, are explicitly scoped to fixed full n-ary trees, so no extension to every alternative model convention is asserted.
The historical literature outside the three deeply inspected close works is not exhaustively indexed; negative finding is based on positive decisive coverage, not absence of other hits.

value.rationale: The purported resolution of an open conjecture with maximal discrepancy is already the main finding of the 2026-11-02 theorem. This is not rejection because the computation is finite or because historical searches are incomplete: it is rejection of a correctly proved but covered and mechanically specialized finding.
